original_question: Let Wn = A5 ≀· · ·≀A5 be the n-times iterated permutational wreath product of A5 in its natural action(so Wn acts on 5n points), and let W = lim Wn be the inverse ←− limit(infinite iterated wreath product of A5). Does W contain a finitely generated dense subgroup of subexponential growth?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.44 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)": "Let W_n = A_5 ≀ ··· ≀ A_5 be the n-times iterated permutational wreath product of A_5 in its natural action (so W_n acts on 5^n points), and let W = lim← W_n be the inverse limit (infinite iterated wreath product of A_5). Does W contain a finitely generated dense subgroup of subexponential growth?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's problem almost verbatim: it identifies the iterated permutational wreath products of A_5, uses the inverse limit W, and asks exactly about the existence of a finitely generated dense subgroup of subexponential growth. It also correctly keeps the scope narrow, with no extra hypotheses or broadenings beyond the problem actually stated in the paper.
missing_details: The paper states that W_n acts on 5^n points, not 5n points.
A_5 is taken in its natural permutation action on a 5-element set.
The inverse limit W should be understood with respect to the natural projection maps W_{n+1} -> W_n.
Density is with respect to the profinite/inverse-limit topology on W.
The subgroup sought is an abstract finitely generated subgroup of W; it is not assumed closed.
'Subexponential growth' refers to the word growth of that finitely generated subgroup with respect to a finite generating set (equivalently, any finite generating set).
refined_question: Let A_5 act naturally on a 5-element set, and for each n >= 1 let W_n be the n-fold iterated permutational wreath product A_5 ≀ A_5 ≀ ··· ≀ A_5 (with n factors), so that W_n acts on 5^n points. Let W = varprojlim_n W_n with respect to the natural projection maps W_{n+1} -> W_n, viewed as a profinite group. Does W contain an abstract subgroup Gamma <= W that is finitely generated, dense in W for the profinite topology, and of subexponential word growth?
justification: The draft is targeting the exact open problem stated as Problem 21.44, not a neighboring statement. In arXiv:1401.0300, this problem appears in the "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" section and is stated almost exactly as in your draft. The only substantive correction needed for paper-faithfulness is that W_n acts on 5^n points, not 5n points. To make the question fully stand-alone, one should also spell out that W is a profinite inverse limit via the natural projection maps, that 'dense' means dense in this profinite topology, and that 'subexponential growth' is the usual growth notion for the finitely generated abstract subgroup. There is no paper-given equivalent reformulation nearby, so none should be added.
